title: UI browser QA from fresh state
description: Browser QA run for sendword from a fresh data directory. Covers authenticated UI routes, hook/script/user management, execution review, approvals, and authenticated API behavior discovered from src/routes and templates. App will be built and run from an isolated tmp working directory with tmp database/logs/scripts.

title: User story: first admin authenticates and exits cleanly
description:
As a first-time sendword operator, I can open a fresh instance, authenticate as the seeded admin, reach the dashboard, use account settings, and log out without dead ends.

Routes: /login, /, /settings, /logout.
Fresh-state setup: create admin user against tmp database before browser run.
Expected: unauthenticated protected pages redirect to login, valid login reaches Hooks dashboard, account menu opens, logout returns to login.

title: Hook auth mode fields stay visible after boosted navigation
description:
Verified with playwright-cli on fresh tmp app at http://127.0.0.1:19090.

Steps:
1. Log in as admin@example.com.
2. From /, click + NEW HOOK.
3. Observe /hooks/new with Auth mode = None (public).
4. Check computed styles: #bearer-fields and #hmac-fields both display block.

Expected: Bearer/HMAC-only fields are hidden when Auth mode is None.
Actual: Both field groups are visible after hx-boost navigation. Running window.toggleAuthFields() manually hides them, so the initial toggle is not firing for boosted page content.

Likely area: templates/hook_form.html inline DOMContentLoaded handler under hx-boost.
close_reason: Fixed and reverified with route tests plus playwright-cli on tmp app

title: Execution replay navigates to /executions/undefined
description:
Verified with playwright-cli on fresh tmp app.

Steps:
1. Create public shell hook smoke-hook with command echo smoke-ok.
2. Trigger POST /hook/smoke-hook.
3. Open /executions/<id>.
4. Click REPLAY.

Expected: replay creates a new execution and navigates to /executions/<new execution id>.
Actual: browser navigates to /executions/undefined.

Evidence: template execution_detail.html parses replay response and uses d.id, while Rust ReplayResponse serializes execution_id. Page URL after click: http://127.0.0.1:19090/executions/undefined.
close_reason: Fixed and reverified with route tests plus playwright-cli on tmp app

title: Successful execution shows stderr panel for empty stderr
description:
Verified with playwright-cli on fresh tmp app.

Steps:
1. Create public shell hook smoke-hook with command echo smoke-ok.
2. Trigger it and open the successful execution detail page.

Expected: no stderr section, or an explicitly empty stderr state, when stderr is empty.
Actual: STDERR panel renders with the fallback text "No output captured." even though the command succeeded and had no stderr.

Likely area: read_log_file returns fallback text for missing/empty stderr, and execution_detail.html renders stderr panel whenever stderr is truthy.
close_reason: Fixed and reverified with route tests plus playwright-cli on tmp app

title: Add user form posts username instead of email
description:
Verified with playwright-cli on fresh tmp app.

Steps:
1. Log in as admin@example.com.
2. Open /admin/users.
3. Fill EMAIL with user2@example.com and PASSWORD with password123.
4. Click ADD USER.

Expected: new user is created or a visible validation error appears.
Actual: the request fails with HTTP 422 and the page remains unchanged. Browser console logs POST /admin/users 422.

Root cause visible in code: templates/users.html names the email input username, but src/routes/settings.rs CreateUserForm expects email.
close_reason: Fixed and reverified with route tests plus playwright-cli on tmp app

title: Trigger attempt validation reason exposes Rust debug formatting
description:
Verified with playwright-cli on fresh tmp app.

Steps:
1. Create hook deploy-filter with payload schema action:string:required.
2. Trigger POST /hook/deploy-filter with bearer auth but missing action.
3. Open hook detail and switch to Trigger Attempts.

Expected: validation attempt reason is written in user-facing language, e.g. "required field action is missing".
Actual: reason shows raw Rust debug output: payload validation failed: [FieldValidationError { field: "action", message: "required field 'action' is missing" }].

Likely area: src/routes/hooks.rs builds trigger_attempt reason with format!("payload validation failed: {errors:?}").
close_reason: Fixed and reverified with route tests plus playwright-cli on tmp app

title: User story: operator manages hook lifecycle
description:
As an operator, I can create a shell webhook from the empty Hooks dashboard, view its details, edit its fields, and delete it when it is no longer needed.

Routes: /, /hooks/new, /hooks/{slug}, /hooks/{slug}/edit, /hooks/{slug}/delete.
Expected: empty state invites creation; form validation is visible; saved hook appears in dashboard and detail view; edits hot-reload sendword.toml; delete returns to dashboard.

title: User story: operator configures advanced hook controls
description:
As an operator, I can configure hook authentication, payload schema, trigger filters, time windows, cooldown/rate limits, retries, cwd, and env vars from the hook form.

Routes: /hooks/new, /hooks/{slug}, /hooks/{slug}/edit.
Expected: bearer/HMAC fields toggle correctly, advanced text formats round-trip through the detail and edit views, invalid formats produce clear errors without losing navigation context.

title: User story: operator reviews and replays executions
description:
As an operator, I can trigger a configured webhook, then review execution status, stdout/stderr logs, details, and replay the execution from the UI.

Routes: POST /hook/{slug}, /hooks/{slug}, /hooks/{slug}/executions, /executions/{id}, /executions/{id}/logs/stream, /executions/{id}/replay.
Expected: successful trigger creates an execution, hook activity updates through HTMX, log output is readable, replay creates a linked execution and navigates to it.

title: User story: operator audits trigger attempts
description:
As an operator, I can see rejected or skipped webhook attempts so I know whether auth, payload validation, filters, cooldowns, or rate limits blocked a trigger.

Routes: POST /hook/{slug}, /hooks/{slug}/attempts.
Expected: auth_failed, validation_failed, filtered, rate_limited, schedule_skipped, and fired attempts render with useful reasons and filters/pagination work.

title: User story: operator manages scripts
description:
As an operator, I can create, edit, save, list, and delete managed scripts, and use a managed script from a hook executor.

Routes: /scripts, /scripts/new, /scripts/{filename}, /scripts/{filename}/delete, /hooks/new, /hooks/{slug}.
Expected: empty state invites script creation; filename validation is clear; saved files become executable in tmp scripts dir; hook detail links back to the script editor when command references it.

title: User story: operator handles approval-gated executions
description:
As an operator, I can review pending approval executions, approve or reject them, and return to execution details to confirm the resulting status.

Routes: /approvals, /executions/{id}/approve, /executions/{id}/reject, /executions/{id}.
Expected: empty approvals state is clear; hooks with approval required create pending rows; approve starts execution; reject marks status rejected and removes pending approval.

title: User story: admin manages users
description:
As an admin, I can list users, add another user, prevent self-deletion, and delete a non-current user.

Routes: /admin/users, /admin/users/{id}/delete.
Expected: current user row is marked YOU; add-user form posts the email and password correctly; duplicate/invalid input errors are visible; self-delete is blocked; deleting another user removes them from the table.

title: User story: operator uses authenticated config and backup APIs
description:
As an authenticated operator, I can export/import portable config JSON and use backup endpoints when backup is configured, while unauthenticated requests are rejected.

Routes: /api/config/export, /api/config/import, /api/backup/list, /api/backup/create, /api/backup/restore.
Expected: config export returns current config; invalid import returns 422 with clear error; backup endpoints return service-unavailable JSON when unconfigured instead of crashing; auth is required.
